project.name: sandbox
project.summary: A simulation of LLM-backed agent populations discussing one topic over K turns under a tunable homophilous neighbour-sampling mechanism, built to measure whether polarization dynamics differ between English and Hinglish discussion and whether injected memes accelerate convergence.

externals.note: Writes a run config YAML and launches a run from the command line.

externals.name: LLM provider
externals.note: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint reached through LiteLLM: self-hosted vLLM, local Ollama, or a hosted API.

externals.name: litellm
externals.note: Third-party client library that normalizes every provider to one async completion call.

Docs/assets/app.js.summary: Viewer for the hand-built documentation site in Docs/. Hash-routed: renders tabs, a filterable file tree and per-file pages out of window.DOCS_DATA, with its own small Python, YAML and JSON syntax highlighters. Not part of the simulation.

Docs/assets/content.js.summary: The hand-written content blob that site renders, a single window.DOCS_DATA assignment. Data, not code: no symbols.

export_csv.py.summary: Flattens a completed campaign into three analysis CSVs: one row per agent-turn with run config joined on, one per agent with its trajectory, and one per run with polarization summaries. Deduplicates the rows an interrupted-and-resumed run logs twice, keeping the later write. Currently the only analysis tooling in the repo.

run_simulation.py.summary: CLI entry point for one run. Loads and validates the config, prints the plan and the LLM-call ceiling, probes a self-hosted endpoint before dispatching anything, then wires the gateway, cost tracker and rate limiter into the orchestrator. Re-running the same config resumes from the last checkpoint instead of starting over.

sandbox/__init__.py.summary: Empty package marker. Declares sandbox as a package and exports nothing.

sandbox/agent_manager.py.summary: Tier 1. Creates and owns the Agent population: assigns personas by cycling the pool, draws each initial stance from the configured scale, and applies a completed Interaction back onto the speaker's stance_history and memory_window. Also provides the deep-copied snapshot and restore used by checkpointing.

sandbox/checkpoint_manager.py.summary: Tier 2. Saves and loads the single per-turn resume point, overwriting rather than appending since only the latest is ever needed. Writes to a .tmp file then atomically renames, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a torn checkpoint. A corrupt checkpoint raises rather than resuming from turn 0.

sandbox/config_loader.py.summary: Tier 0. Reads a run config YAML, validates it into an ExperimentRun, and confirms the persona and meme pools it names exist on disk. Accumulates schema errors and missing-asset errors into one ConfigLoadError rather than failing on the first, and stamps git_commit_hash from the working tree so a config cannot claim a commit it did not run against.

sandbox/cost_tracker.py.summary: Tier 0. Converts token counts into dollars against pricing_table.yaml and enforces the run's cost ceiling. A missing pricing entry raises rather than falling back to an estimate. record() is synchronous by design even though ModelGateway.generate() is async.

sandbox/interaction_engine.py.summary: Tier 2. Neighbour selection by Ohagi's alpha-sampling: alpha blends uniform random choice against stance-distance-weighted homophily, drawn without replacement by Efraimidis-Spirakis reservoir sampling. Invalid alpha, N, population size or sampling weight raises rather than being clamped, since a silent clamp would be the exact confound the design warns about.

sandbox/logging_writer.py.summary: Tier 2. Append-only run persistence: one JSON line per interaction under an asyncio lock, plus the run config at start and final agent state at completion. Does not create the run directory and does not catch disk errors, both deliberately.

sandbox/meme_pool_manager.py.summary: Tier 1. Loads a meme dataset and decides, per scheduled speaker per turn, whether that speaker's post is a meme instead of a generated reply. Resolution must happen in the frozen snapshot phase before any dispatch. get_meme resolves an id back to content, since Interaction stores only the id.

sandbox/model_gateway.py.summary: Tier 1. The single async interface to every LLM provider, backed by LiteLLM. Classifies provider errors into retryable and fatal, retries the former three times with exponential backoff, measures latency itself, records cost, and caps simultaneous in-flight requests with a semaphore. Vision support is a static table lookup that raises on an unrecognized model id.

sandbox/models.py.summary: Tier 0. Every Pydantic model the system shares: Agent, Interaction, ExperimentRun, MemeContent, MemeInjectionConfig, StanceRecord and CheckpointState. Validation lives here rather than in calling code, through regex-constrained string fields and cross-field model validators. ExperimentRun and MemeInjectionConfig set extra=forbid so a typo'd YAML key raises instead of silently leaving a mechanism switched off.

sandbox/prompt_builder.py.summary: Tier 3. Assembles one speaker's prompt from persona, topic, current position, its own recent reasoning, and the sampled neighbours' latest posts. Exactly one directive line varies across language conditions so RQ1's comparison is not confounded by prompt shape. Attaches at most one meme image and degrades the rest to captions. No design document specifies this module.

sandbox/rate_limiter.py.summary: Tier 0. Per-provider minimum-interval throttle shared across all concurrent dispatch tasks. An unconfigured provider is unlimited, and a configured limit of 0 means no limit rather than no requests. release() is a deliberate no-op kept for call-site symmetry.

sandbox/seed_manager.py.summary: Tier 0. Hands out seeded random.Random streams so no stochastic choice ever touches the global random module. Three long-lived streams are offset from the base seed by 0, 1 and 2; turn_rng derives a fresh stream per (purpose, turn) so a resumed turn draws exactly what an uninterrupted one would.

sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py.summary: Tier 3. The per-turn loop and the only module that touches every other component. Freezes a snapshot, resolves neighbours and meme injections to completion, dispatches all M agents concurrently, then applies results. Absorbs StanceParseFailure and FatalGatewayError into a failed_logged_null row for that one agent while anything else aborts the run, and resumes from a checkpoint by rebuilding each agent's last post from the log.

sandbox/stance_parser.py.summary: Tier 2. Pure stateless extraction of (stance_value, reason_text) from raw model output via a STANCE: <number> regex, plus a range check against the configured scale. Holds no retry logic and cannot reach the gateway; the orchestrator owns the retry loop.

sandbox/vision_fallback.py.summary: Tier 2. Builds the prompt text for a meme, with the image bytes when the receiving backend supports vision and caption-only text when it does not. The single place in the codebase that frames meme content, so the instruction wording is identical either way and only the payload differs.

tests/__init__.py.summary: Empty package marker, so tests/ is importable and tests.factories resolves.

tests/conftest.py.summary: Shared pytest fixtures: a valid config dict, a helper that writes a config dict to a YAML file under tmp_path, and an autospec'd ModelGateway double returning a parseable stance reply. Autospec is kept rather than replaced with a bare AsyncMock so a real signature change breaks the tests instead of silently passing.

tests/factories.py.summary: Plain-function data builders for ExperimentRun, Agent, Interaction, a correctly formatted model reply, and a BackendResponse. Functions rather than fixtures deliberately, since fixtures cannot be used inside parametrize. Each takes **overrides passed straight to the model constructor.

tests/test_agent_manager.py.summary: Population creation, persona cycling past the pool size, seeded stance reproducibility, the memory_window cap, and snapshot/restore isolation.

tests/test_checkpoint_manager.py.summary: Save and load round-tripping, that a second save leaves only the latest, that a corrupt checkpoint raises, and that no .tmp file survives a successful write.

tests/test_config_loader.py.summary: Every config rejection path, including that two independent errors both surface in one ConfigLoadError, that YAML-supplied git_commit_hash is ignored, and that unknown keys are named.

tests/test_cost_tracker.py.summary: Cost arithmetic and accumulation, that an unpriced combination raises instead of charging zero, ceiling behaviour, and that concurrent record() calls lose no updates.

tests/test_factories.py.summary: The builders themselves: that their defaults validate, that overrides still go through validation, and that the mock gateway both returns a parseable reply and rejects calls breaking the real signature.

tests/test_integration_run.py.summary: End to end, YAML on disk to interactions.jsonl: the shipped example config loads, a full run writes correct output, the same seed reproduces a run exactly, a resumed run matches an uninterrupted one, and agent state agrees with the log.

tests/test_interaction_engine.py.summary: Alpha extremes (homophilous at 1, roughly uniform at 0), the N-distinct-never-self contract, seeded reproducibility, and that zero, negative, NaN and mismatched sampling weights all raise.

tests/test_logging_writer.py.summary: That concurrent appends produce N untorn parseable lines, that both one-shot writes round-trip through their models, that agents_final overwrites, and that a missing run_dir raises.

tests/test_meme_pool_manager.py.summary: Injection decisioning across disabled, rate 0, rate 1 and fixed-turn schedules, seeded reproducibility, the empty and missing pool error paths, and that every image path in the real pool resolves on disk.

tests/test_model_gateway.py.summary: Retry versus fatal classification, construction-time vision resolution, cost recording with the bare model id and correct modality, that latency is measured rather than read off the response, api_base forwarding, and that the concurrency cap holds including across retries.

tests/test_models.py.summary: Schema-level guarantees: the memory_window cap on construction and on assignment, that in-place append bypasses it, extra=forbid on both config models, and that a stance_scale of two identical values is rejected.

tests/test_prompt_builder.py.summary: That the three language conditions differ only in the directive line and stay within a bounded length spread, the Fix A five-turn memory slice, turn-1 neighbour omission, the one-image meme rule and its downgrade flag, and that a retry changes only the format block.

tests/test_rate_limiter.py.summary: Interval spacing, that an unconfigured provider returns immediately, that concurrent acquires for one provider serialize, and that a limit of 0 means no limit rather than a division by zero.

tests/test_seed_manager.py.summary: That one seed reproduces each stream, that the three streams never correlate, that a property returns the same advancing instance, and that turn_rng is a pure function of seed, purpose and turn so a resume replays nothing.

tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py.summary: The widest file: per-turn row counts and neighbour shape, seeded reproducibility, meme turns costing no call, the parse-retry and fatal-error paths, cost-ceiling and unexpected-exception aborts, checkpoint intervals, resume, and that no agent sees another's same-turn output.

tests/test_stance_parser.py.summary: Well-formed and malformed STANCE lines, case insensitivity, negative and decimal values, that the first of several matches wins while all are stripped from reason_text, and the scale range checks.

tests/test_vision_fallback.py.summary: That a vision receiver gets matching image bytes, that a text-only receiver gets the caption woven in with no image, and that the text-only path never touches the filesystem even for a nonexistent image.

functions.export_csv.py::load_run: Reads one run directory's interactions.jsonl and joins the run-level config fields onto every row, plus a topic_key parsed from the directory name and a row_index recording write order. Returns None when the directory lacks either file or the log is empty.
functions.export_csv.py::mark_duplicates: Sorts by write order and flags all but the final write of each (run_id, turn, speaker_agent_id). Keeping the last is what makes the surviving row the post-resume copy.
functions.export_csv.py::derive: Adds the columns every analysis would otherwise recompute: signed and absolute stance shift, whether the agent moved, analysis validity, neighbour count, and reason character and word counts. Also joins neighbour ids into a pipe-delimited string, since lists do not survive a CSV round-trip.
functions.export_csv.py::agents_table: Builds one row per agent per run from valid rows only: turns completed, total absolute movement, mean shift, turns moved, mean token counts, and first and last stance. Reports net_drift separately from total movement, because an agent can move a great deal and end where it began.
functions.export_csv.py::runs_table: Builds one row per run: the config, interaction and failure counts, parse failure rate, mean latency and tokens, and the polarization measures. final_stance_std is the headline figure, and polarization_change is its gain over the initial spread.
functions.export_csv.py::main: Walks the campaign directory, skipping excluded run ids and unusable directories, concatenates every run, marks and by default drops re-logged rows with a report, then writes interactions.csv, agents.csv and runs.csv and prints each file's shape. Returns 1 when the path is not a directory or no runs loaded.
functions.run_simulation.py::describe: Prints the run's identity, population parameters, model and output path, plus the worst-case LLM call count as M times K. Warns when a hosted_vllm model has no api_base, since litellm would route on the prefix and never reach the server, and notes when a checkpoint exists so the user knows this resumes.
functions.run_simulation.py::check_server: Probes a self-hosted endpoint before anything is dispatched, using Ollama's or vLLM's listing path as appropriate, and checks that the served name matches the configured one. Returns an error string with a start-the-server hint, or None. Exists because a connection error is classed as transient, so without this every agent retries three times with backoff and the real cause ends up buried.
functions.run_simulation.py::launch: Builds the cost tracker, gateway and rate limiter, runs the orchestrator to completion, then reports the interaction count and what each output file holds.
functions.run_simulation.py::main: Parses the config path, --dry-run and --runs-dir, loads the config and prints the plan, returning 1 on a config error. Then probes the server, runs the simulation, and maps outcomes to exit codes: 0 success, 1 config or server problem, 2 run failure, 130 interrupt, each with a reminder that the last completed turn is checkpointed.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager: Creates and owns the run's Agent population in an id-keyed dict, and is the only writer of agent state during a run.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager._: Stores the run, the persona-assignment RNG and an empty agent dict. Creates no agents until initialize_population is called.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager.i: Creates run.M agents with ids agent_0000 upward, cycling the persona pool when M exceeds its size, and drawing each initial stance from the configured scale. Deterministic given the same seed because persona then stance is always consumed in that order.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager._: Reads data/personas/<persona_pool_id>.jsonl as plain text, one persona per non-blank line. Raises FileNotFoundError rather than trusting the config loader's earlier existence check.
Draws one value uniformly from run.stance_scale using the injected RNG, never the global random module.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager.g: Returns the agent by id, letting KeyError propagate. An unknown id is treated as a programmer error, so it is not wrapped.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager.a: Returns a new list of the live Agent objects. The objects themselves are not copied, which is why the orchestrator's frozen snapshot is a convention rather than a guarantee.

Appends a StanceRecord built from the interaction to the speaker's stance_history, then recomputes memory_window as that agent's own last 5 interaction_ids. Called only after a turn's dispatch has fully completed.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager.s: Returns a deep copy of every agent, so later mutation of the manager cannot reach the checkpoint that was saved.
functions.sandbox/agent_manager.py::AgentManager.r: Rebuilds the internal dict from a list of agents, deep-copying on the way in so later mutation cannot reach back into the caller's list.
functions.sandbox/checkpoint_manager.py::Checkpoin: Saves and loads the single resume point per run, under runs/<run_id>/checkpoints/.
Stores the runs directory root. Creates nothing until save is called.

Creates the checkpoints directory if needed, serializes the state to latest.json.tmp, then atomically renames it over latest.json so a crash mid-write cannot leave a torn file. Overwrites rather than appending, since only the latest is ever read.

Returns None when no checkpoint exists, which is how a fresh run is detected. A checkpoint that exists but fails schema validation raises uncaught, rather than silently restarting at turn 0 and discarding completed work.
functions.sandbox/config_loader.py::ConfigLoadErro: Raised for any config problem. Carries the config path and the full list of accumulated error strings, so one raise can report every problem at once.
Stores the config path and the accumulated error list, and builds a message joining every error with semicolons.
functions.sandbox/config_loader.py::load_run_confi: Reads a YAML file, stamps git_commit_hash from the working tree, validates against ExperimentRun, and checks that the persona and meme pools it names exist. Accumulates schema and filesystem errors into a single ConfigLoadError; never returns a partially valid run.
functions.sandbox/config_loader.py::_format_valida: Turns Pydantic errors into 'field: message' strings, and rewrites extra_forbidden into a typo hint. Raw error dicts repeat the whole input payload once per error, which buried the actual problems.
functions.sandbox/config_loader.py::_resolve_git_c: Returns the current HEAD via git rev-parse. Raises ConfigLoadError with a placeholder path if the directory is not a repo or has no commits, so an unreproducible run is rejected rather than recorded with an empty hash.
functions.sandbox/config_loader.py::_referenced_as: Returns every missing-asset error for the referenced persona pool and, when memes are enabled, the meme pool. Reads the raw dict rather than a validated model so it runs even when schema validation already failed.
functions.sandbox/cost_tracker.py::CostCeilingExce: Raised when the accumulated cost reaches or passes the run's max_cost_usd. Carries the current total and the ceiling. Fatal to the run by design.
Stores the current total and the ceiling and formats both into the message, so the breach is legible without re-reading the tracker.
functions.sandbox/cost_tracker.py::CostTracker: Accumulates dollar cost across a run against a pricing table loaded at construction, and enforces the ceiling. Raises FileNotFoundError immediately if the pricing table is absent.
functions.sandbox/cost_tracker.py::CostTracker.__i: Loads and parses pricing_table.yaml, zeroes the total, and creates a threading.Lock. The lock is defence in depth against a future await inside record(), not a current requirement.
functions.sandbox/cost_tracker.py::CostTracker.rec: Looks up the per-1k rates, adds the cost for this call to the running total, then raises CostCeilingExceeded if the total has reached the ceiling. The call that crosses the ceiling is always counted, deliberately. Synchronous, and called without await from async code.
functions.sandbox/cost_tracker.py::CostTracker._lo: Indexes the pricing table by provider, model id and modality. Raises ValueError naming the missing combination rather than returning an estimated or zero rate.
functions.sandbox/cost_tracker.py::CostTracker.tot: The accumulated cost so far, read by the orchestrator when it finalizes the run record.
functions.sandbox/interaction_engine.py::Recommend: Protocol for neighbour selection. Any implementation must return exactly N distinct agents and never include the speaker, which is what lets the orchestrator depend on the interface rather than on AlphaSampling.
The protocol method: given a speaker, the population, the turn and an RNG, return that speaker's N neighbours for this turn.
functions.sandbox/interaction_engine.py::AlphaSamp: Ohagi's echo-chamber mechanism. alpha of 0 samples uniformly at random, alpha of 1 weights entirely by closeness of stance, and values between blend the two.

Validates and stores alpha and N. Raises ValueError for alpha outside [0,1] or N below 1 rather than clamping, since a silent clamp would itself be the implementation-level confound the design warns against.

Excludes the speaker, raises ValueError if fewer than N candidates remain, then weights each candidate by alpha/(1+stance distance) plus (1-alpha) and draws N without replacement from the injected RNG.
functions.sandbox/interaction_engine.py::_current_: Reads an agent's stance as of the end of the previous turn: initial_stance at turn 1 or with no history, otherwise the last stance_history value. Deliberately duplicates Agent.current_stance rather than calling it, to stay a direct port of the spec.
functions.sandbox/interaction_engine.py::_weighted: Efraimidis-Spirakis weighted reservoir sampling, deterministic given the RNG state. Rejects a length mismatch and any non-finite or non-positive weight: the key formula divides by the weight, so 0 raises, and a negative weight would make an item sort first and always be selected, a silent wrong answer in the module whose contract is to never clamp.
functions.sandbox/logging_writer.py::LoggingWriter: Writes one run's three output files. Holds an asyncio.Lock that serializes the concurrent interaction appends coming from a turn's dispatch tasks.
Stores the run directory, precomputes the interactions path, and creates the append lock. Does not create the directory: the orchestrator is expected to have done so.

Appends one JSON line under the lock. Locks rather than relying on OS append atomicity, since concurrent task writes through one handle in a single process are not guaranteed untorn. Disk errors propagate, because silently losing a row would corrupt the dataset undetectably.
Writes run_config.json. Called at run start and again at finalize, with no locking since neither call overlaps concurrent activity.
Writes one JSON line per agent to agents_final.jsonl in overwrite mode, once at completion. A second call leaves only the second list's contents.
functions.sandbox/meme_pool_manager.py::MemePoolMa: Loads a meme pool when injection is enabled and decides which scheduled speakers post a meme each turn. Holds the pool as a list for sampling and a dict for id lookup.
Stores the config and RNG, and loads the pool only when injection is enabled, so a disabled run never touches the filesystem.
Parses data/memes/<meme_pool_id>.jsonl into MemeContent records, one per non-blank line. Raises FileNotFoundError for a missing file and ValueError for a file that parses to nothing.

Resolves a meme_id back to its MemeContent. Raises KeyError on an unknown id, because an id in the log that is not in the pool means the data and the pool disagree, which is a integrity failure rather than a missing value.

Returns agent_id to MemeContent or None for every scheduled speaker, drawing independently per agent at the configured rate under the random schedule, or only on configured turns under fixed_turn. Takes an optional rng that overrides the construction-time stream, which is how the orchestrator passes a per-turn stream that survives a resume. Must run before any dispatch.
True for every turn under the random schedule, and only for configured turns under fixed_turn. Raises ValueError on an unrecognized schedule.
Picks one meme uniformly from the pool using the passed stream, or the construction-time one.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::TransientGatew: Wraps a provider error judged retryable: timeouts, rate limits and connection failures. Retried up to three times with exponential backoff.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::FatalGatewayEr: Wraps a provider error judged non-retryable: authentication failure, an invalid model id, a rejected request. Never retried, and absorbed by the orchestrator into a failed row for that one agent.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::BackendRespons: One normalized provider reply: the text, prompt and completion token counts, a locally measured latency, and the full raw response dict.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ModelGateway: The single async interface to every provider, via LiteLLM. Resolves vision support once at construction, optionally bounds in-flight requests with a semaphore, and routes self-hosted traffic through an explicit api_base.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ModelGateway._: Resolves supports_vision from the static table, stores the rate limiter and cost tracker, and builds a semaphore when max_concurrency is given. The cap matters because the orchestrator dispatches all M agents at once: against a local vLLM with a smaller batch size, the surplus connections accumulate until the server starts closing them and the run dies while the server is still healthy.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ModelGateway.g: Takes a concurrency slot, acquires the provider's rate limit, calls the provider with retries, then records cost using the bare model id and the right modality. Does not itself perform vision fallback: the caller must already have substituted a caption-only prompt for a text-only backend.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ModelGateway._: Issues the litellm.acompletion call and maps provider exceptions onto the transient or fatal taxonomy. Measures latency with a monotonic clock rather than reading it off the response, because the field the design doc's sample reads does not exist and the resulting AttributeError would abort the whole run on the first successful call.
Returns the semaphore when a cap is configured, otherwise a no-op async context manager. Held across the entire call including retries, so a retrying agent adds no connection beyond the cap.
Returns the part of model_backend_id before the first slash, defaulting to openai when there is no prefix.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_null_slot: An async context manager that yields immediately, standing in for the semaphore when concurrency is unbounded.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_bare_model_id: Strips any provider prefix, so anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 becomes claude-sonnet-4-6. Both the vision table and the pricing table are keyed by bare ids, so every lookup normalizes through here.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_resolve_visio: Looks the bare model id up in the vision-capable and text-only sets. Raises ValueError on an unrecognized id rather than defaulting to text-only, which could silently misclassify a vision model.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_build_message: Builds the messages payload: a plain string for text, or a text part plus a base64 data-URI image part when image bytes are supplied.
functions.sandbox/models.py::StanceRecord: One entry in an agent's stance history: the turn, the stance it moved to, the reasoning text, and the interaction_id that produced it. Turn is constrained to 1 or greater.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Agent: One simulated participant and all of its state: persona, language condition, backend id, initial stance, full stance_history, and a memory_window capped at 5 entries. Sets validate_assignment so the cap is re-checked on assignment rather than enforced only by convention.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Agent.current_stance: Returns the stance_value of the last stance_history entry, or initial_stance when the history is empty.
functions.sandbox/models.py::MemeContent: One meme from a labeled dataset: id, image path, caption, a stance label used directly as the poster's stance, an optional offensiveness label, and the source dataset name.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Interaction: One agent-turn as logged: speaker, the neighbours it was shown, stance before and after, reason text, whether the post was generated text or a meme, token counts, latency, and an api_call_status of success, retried_success or failed_logged_null.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Interaction.check_mem: Rejects a row whose content_type and meme_id disagree: a meme row needs a non-null meme_id, and a generated_text row needs a null one. Runs after field validation.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Interaction.is_valid_: True unless api_call_status is failed_logged_null. The one place the exclusion rule is expressed, read by both the orchestrator and export_csv.py.
functions.sandbox/models.py::MemeInjectionConfig: The meme block of a run config: whether injection is on, which pool, the per-agent-turn rate, and a random or fixed_turn schedule. Forbids unknown keys because a typo here silently disables the mechanism RQ3 manipulates.
functions.sandbox/models.py::MemeInjectionConfig.c: When enabled, requires a meme_pool_id, and requires fixed_turns to be non-empty under the fixed_turn schedule. Raises rather than quietly injecting nothing.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun: The full validated run config and the run's lifecycle record: topic, alpha, M, N, K, language condition, model and endpoint, stance scale with its anchor labels, seed, temperature, cost ceiling, plus status, timestamps and total cost written back at the end. Forbids unknown keys.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun.check_n: Rejects N greater than or equal to M, since a speaker cannot have as many distinct neighbours as there are agents including itself.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun.check_s: Rejects a stance_scale with fewer than 2 distinct values. The field's own length check counts entries, so [3, 3] passed and then made every reply but one unparseable, failing the whole population.
functions.sandbox/models.py::CheckpointState: A resume point: the run id, the last fully completed turn, and a deep copy of every agent. Carries no interaction content, which is why a resume rebuilds last posts from the log.
functions.sandbox/prompt_builder.py::BuiltPrompt: What the orchestrator hands to the gateway: the prompt text, optional image bytes, and used_vision_fallback. That flag is wider than its original meaning, answering 'did this agent see less than the full meme content it was shown', which covers both a text-only backend and the second meme in a turn that one image slot cannot carry.
functions.sandbox/prompt_builder.py::PromptBuilder: Assembles one speaker's prompt for one turn. Holds the run, the backend's vision support and a meme lookup callable, and precomputes the scale endpoints.

Stores its collaborators and the scale bounds, raising ValueError for a language condition with no directive. Unreachable through ExperimentRun's own regex, kept so a misconfigured run cannot silently render as a valid English one.

Builds the full prompt from persona, topic, current position, the agent's own recent reasoning, the neighbours' latest posts, the language directive and the output format block, joined by blank lines. Takes neighbour posts as Interactions rather than Agents because only Interaction carries content_type and meme_id. Reads nothing from the current turn, which is what makes the frozen-snapshot guarantee hold.
Renders the agent's current stance against the scale endpoints and their configured anchor labels, so a bare number means the same thing to every agent on every turn.

Renders the agent's own last 5 stance_history entries as turn, position and reasoning, or an empty string when there is no history. The slice is the memory cap that actually reaches the model, since neither the schema nor the manager can catch an in-place append.

Renders each sampled neighbour's most recent post, with meme posts framed through vision_fallback and only the one whose image is attached getting the multimodal framing. Omitted entirely on turn 1, when showing bare initial stances with no reasoning would be a stimulus with no analogue in any later turn.

Renders the output contract the parser depends on: one STANCE line first, the number on that line only. On a retry it prepends an emphatic warning and changes nothing else, so a retried reply is still a response to the same stimulus.

Decides which single image is attached, since the gateway takes one image but N neighbours may include several memes. Attaches the first meme-bearing neighbour in the reproducible neighbour order and returns a flag when any other meme had to degrade to its caption.
Returns the speaker_agent_id of the first meme post in neighbour order, or None. Identifies which neighbour gets the attached image.
functions.sandbox/prompt_builder.py::_fmt: Renders a whole-number stance as an integer and leaves a fractional one alone, so both drawn and model-returned values read naturally in a prompt.
functions.sandbox/prompt_builder.py::_indent: Prefixes every non-empty line with four spaces, used to nest a rendered meme body under its neighbour header.
functions.sandbox/rate_limiter.py::RateLimiter: Per-provider minimum-interval throttle, one instance shared by every concurrent dispatch task. Precomputes 60/limit as the interval and holds one asyncio.Lock per configured provider.
functions.sandbox/rate_limiter.py::RateLimiter.__i: Builds the per-provider interval and lock maps. A limit of 0 becomes a 0-second interval, meaning no limit, since 0 requests per minute would make the provider unusable and is almost certainly a config mistake.
functions.sandbox/rate_limiter.py::RateLimiter.acq: Returns immediately for an unconfigured provider. Otherwise takes that provider's lock, sleeps for whatever remains of the minimum interval since the last request, and records the new timestamp.
functions.sandbox/rate_limiter.py::RateLimiter.rel: Deliberate no-op. An interval-based strategy needs no release step; the method exists so the gateway's call site can pair acquire with release.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager: Owns one run's randomness. Builds three long-lived random.Random instances at seed, seed+1 and seed+2 so the neighbour, meme and persona streams never correlate, and derives per-turn streams on demand.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.__i: Stores the base seed and constructs the three offset streams. Each property hands back the same advancing instance, never a fresh one.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.nei: The long-lived stream for neighbour selection, seeded at the base seed.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.mem: The long-lived stream for meme injection decisions, seeded at base seed plus 1.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.per: The long-lived stream for persona assignment and initial stance draws, seeded at base seed plus 2.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.tur: Returns a fresh stream that is a pure function of (seed, purpose, turn), using large distinct purpose offsets. Exists because the long-lived streams cannot survive a resume: their position is not checkpointed, so a resumed run would replay an earlier turn's draws. Raises ValueError on an unknown purpose or a turn below 1.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::Simu: The per-turn loop and the only component that holds every other one. Owns the run lifecycle, the per-turn ordering that keeps runs reproducible, and the map of each agent's most recent post that becomes the next turn's stimulus.
Stores every collaborator, the run directory, and an empty last-posts map. Takes the SeedManager rather than individual streams because per-turn streams are derived from it.

Creates the run directory, then either resumes from a checkpoint or initializes the population and writes the run config. Loops turns to K, checkpointing on the configured interval, and checkpoints a final turn the interval would have skipped. On any escaping exception it records failed_partial or failed_total and re-raises; on success it writes agents_final and marks the run completed.

One turn in the exact required order: derive the two per-turn streams, resolve every agent's neighbours, then resolve meme injections, then copy the last-posts map, then dispatch all agents concurrently with return_exceptions. Afterwards it logs every row, re-raises anything unexpected, and applies only usable results to agent state. Neighbour and meme resolution are sequential with respect to each other because a single Random is not safe under concurrent use.

Produces one agent's Interaction. A meme speaker short-circuits with no LLM call. Otherwise it builds the prompt, caches the two possible variants so a retry does not re-read the meme image from disk, and tries up to three times: a parse failure flips only the format emphasis, a fatal gateway error returns a failed row immediately, and an exhausted budget returns a failed row too.
Closure that builds and caches a prompt per emphasize_format value. Only two prompts exist across the retry budget, so rebuilding per attempt re-read the meme image from disk for no benefit.

Builds the Interaction for a meme turn, using the dataset stance_label as the stance and the caption as the reason text, with zero tokens and zero latency. used_vision_fallback is False by definition, since that field describes what a receiver saw of someone else's meme and a posting turn builds no prompt.

Builds a failed_logged_null row whose stance_after repeats stance_before and whose reason_text is empty. Never fabricates a placeholder stance; because no StanceRecord follows, later turns keep reading the agent's last known value.

Replays interactions.jsonl after a resume to recover each agent's most recent usable post, keeping the highest turn per speaker and skipping failed rows. Needed because the checkpoint carries only agent state and StanceRecord has no content_type, so agent state alone cannot say whether a past post was a meme, and a resumed run would otherwise render every previous meme as ordinary text.
Saves a deep-copied agent snapshot for the given turn.
Sets the terminal status and completion timestamp, copies in the total cost when a tracker is present, and rewrites run_config.json. The one record that is mutated and rewritten rather than appended.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::buil: Wires a full orchestrator from a validated run and a gateway, constructing the SeedManager and handing each consumer its own stream. Exists so that routing lives in exactly one place: giving a consumer the wrong stream yields a run that still completes deterministically but is no longer the run the config describes, which is close to undetectable afterwards.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::_cur: Returns the stance to log as stance_before, mirroring the interaction engine's reading exactly. Duplicated deliberately: if the two disagreed, stance_before would not be the value neighbour sampling actually used and every regression fitted on that column would be wrong.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::_now: Returns the current UTC time as a second-precision ISO string with a trailing Z, used for every timestamp the run writes.
functions.sandbox/stance_parser.py::StanceParseFai: Raised when no stance can be read from a reply, or the value falls outside the configured scale. Caught only by the orchestrator, which retries with a louder format block.
functions.sandbox/stance_parser.py::parse_stance: Finds the first case-insensitive 'STANCE: <number>' match and returns its value plus the reasoning text. Strips every such occurrence from the reason, not just the one it read, so a restated stance cannot leak into the field the RQ2 analyses consume. Raises StanceParseFailure when no line matches or the value is not numeric.
functions.sandbox/stance_parser.py::clamp_and_vali: Returns the value unchanged if it lies within the scale's endpoints, and raises StanceParseFailure otherwise. Despite the name it never clamps: an out-of-range value is treated exactly like an unparseable one.
functions.sandbox/vision_fallback.py::build_meme_p: Returns the prompt text and, for a vision-capable receiver, the image bytes. A text-only receiver gets the caption woven into the text and no image, and the filesystem is never touched in that branch. The instruction framing is identical either way, so only the payload differs.
functions.sandbox/vision_fallback.py::_load_image: Reads the meme image from disk, raising FileNotFoundError on a missing file. Treated as a meme-pool integrity problem rather than something to degrade around.
functions.tests/conftest.py::_base_config_dict: Returns a minimal valid config dict: M=10, N=3, K=2, a 7-point stance scale, the 4-entry test persona pool and seed 42. The single source both config fixtures build on.
functions.tests/conftest.py::valid_config_dict: Fixture handing out a fresh copy of that valid config dict per test.
functions.tests/conftest.py::write_config: Fixture returning a helper that dumps a config dict to YAML under tmp_path and returns the path.
functions.tests/conftest.py::write_config._write: The returned helper: writes the dict as YAML to the named file under tmp_path and returns its Path.
functions.tests/conftest.py::mock_gateway: Fixture giving an autospec'd ModelGateway that returns a parseable stance reply. Only the return value is set, never generate itself, so the signature enforcement autospec provides is preserved. supports_vision and model_backend_id are assigned explicitly because autospec cannot see instance attributes.
functions.tests/conftest.py::text_only_gateway: The same double with supports_vision False and a text-only model id, for exercising the vision-fallback path.
functions.tests/factories.py::make_run: Builds a valid ExperimentRun defaulting to M=10, N=3, K=2 against the test persona pool with memes disabled. Overrides pass straight to the constructor, so they still go through validation.

functions.tests/factories.py::make_interaction: Builds a successful generated-text Interaction. A meme row needs both content_type and meme_id, since the model's validator requires them to agree.

    CLI->>CLI: describe(run, runs_dir)

sequences.title: SimulationOrchestrator: one turn under Fix F
sequences.summary: Neighbour and meme resolution both finish before any dispatch starts, and all state mutation waits until gather returns.
sequences.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant ORCH as SimulationOrchestrator
    participant AM as AgentManager
    participant SM as SeedManager
    participant IE as AlphaSampling
    participant MM as MemePoolManager
    participant LW as LoggingWriter
    participant CM as CheckpointManager

    ORCH->>AM: all_agents()
    AM-->>ORCH: live Agent references
    Note over ORCH: frozen snapshot phase, nothing dispatched yet
    ORCH->>SM: turn_rng("neighbor", turn)
    SM-->>ORCH: stream derived from seed, purpose and turn
    ORCH->>SM: turn_rng("meme", turn)
    SM-->>ORCH: independent stream
    loop every agent
        ORCH->>IE: select_neighbors(agent, all_agents, turn, rng)
        IE-->>ORCH: N distinct agents, never the speaker
    end
    ORCH->>MM: resolve_injections_for_turn(all_agents, turn, rng)
    MM-->>ORCH: agent_id to MemeContent or None
    Note over ORCH: copy _last_posts into frozen_posts
    Note over ORCH: dispatch phase, all M agents concurrently
    par every agent
        ORCH->>ORCH: _process_one_agent_turn(...)
    end
    Note over ORCH: step 6, the only place state changes
    loop every result
        alt unexpected exception
            Note over ORCH: re-raise, aborting the run
        else Interaction
            ORCH->>LW: write_interaction(result)
            alt failed_logged_null
                Note over ORCH: logged but excluded, no stance_history entry
            else usable
                ORCH->>AM: apply_interaction(agent_id, result)
                Note over ORCH: _last_posts[agent_id] = result
            end
        end
    end
    ORCH->>CM: save(run_id, turn, snapshot)

sequences.title: One agent's turn: prompt, dispatch, parse, retry
sequences.summary: A meme turn short-circuits with no LLM call; a text turn gets three attempts, with only the format block changing on retry.
sequences.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant ORCH as SimulationOrchestrator
    participant PB as PromptBuilder
    participant VF as vision_fallback.py
    participant GW as ModelGateway
    participant RL as RateLimiter
    participant LLM as LLM provider
    participant CT as CostTracker
    participant SP as stance_parser.py

    alt meme speaker
        ORCH->>ORCH: _build_meme_interaction(...)
        Note over ORCH: dataset stance_label is the stance, zero tokens, zero latency
    else generated text
        loop up to MAX_STANCE_ATTEMPTS
            ORCH->>PB: build_discussion_prompt(agent, neighbor_posts, turn, emphasize_format)
            PB->>VF: build_meme_prompt(meme, receiver_supports_vision)
            VF-->>PB: caption text, and image bytes only for a vision receiver
            PB-->>ORCH: BuiltPrompt with text, optional image, used_vision_fallback
            ORCH->>GW: generate(text, image, temperature)
            GW->>RL: acquire(provider)
            GW->>LLM: acompletion via litellm
            alt transient error
                LLM-->>GW: timeout, 429 or 5xx
                GW->>LLM: retry, exponential backoff, up to 3 attempts
            end
            LLM-->>GW: completion with usage
            GW->>CT: record(provider, bare model_id, modality, tokens)
            GW-->>ORCH: BackendResponse
            ORCH->>SP: parse_stance(response.text)
            alt no STANCE line, or out of scale
                SP-->>ORCH: StanceParseFailure
                Note over ORCH: emphasize_format = True, nothing else changes
            else parsed
                SP-->>ORCH: stance_value, reason_text
                Note over ORCH: Interaction built, status success or retried_success
            end
        end
        Note over ORCH: budget exhausted or FatalGatewayError
        ORCH->>ORCH: _failed_interaction(...), stance repeats stance_before
    end

sequences.title: Resuming an interrupted run
sequences.summary: Agent state comes from the checkpoint, but each agent's last post is rebuilt from the log, because StanceRecord cannot say whether a post was a meme.
sequences.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant ORCH as SimulationOrchestrator
    participant CM as CheckpointManager
    participant CK as latest.json
    participant LOG as interactions.jsonl
    participant AM as AgentManager
    participant LW as LoggingWriter

    ORCH->>CM: load(run_id)
    CM->>CK: read latest.json
    alt no checkpoint
        CK-->>CM: missing
        CM-->>ORCH: None
        ORCH->>AM: initialize_population()
        ORCH->>LW: write_run_config(run)
        Note over ORCH: start_turn = 1, status running
    else checkpoint present
        CK-->>CM: CheckpointState
        CM-->>ORCH: last_completed_turn, agent_snapshot
        ORCH->>AM: restore_from_snapshot(agent_snapshot)
        ORCH->>ORCH: _rebuild_last_posts()
        ORCH->>LOG: read every line
        LOG-->>ORCH: Interaction rows through last_completed_turn
        Note over ORCH: failed rows skipped, so neighbours see the same last real post
    end
    loop turn in start_turn..K
        ORCH->>ORCH: _run_turn(turn)
        ORCH->>CM: save(run_id, turn, snapshot) on the configured interval
    end
    Note over ORCH: a final turn the interval skipped is checkpointed anyway
    ORCH->>LW: write_agents_final(all_agents)
    ORCH->>ORCH: _finalize("completed")

groups.summary: Population creation, persona cycling past the pool size, seeded stance reproducibility, the memory_window cap, and snapshot/restore isolation.

tests.summary: With M larger than the pool, personas repeat in order, so each persona is shared by several agents rather than running out.
Two managers with identically seeded RNGs draw the same initial stances in the same order.
An unknown agent id raises KeyError uncaught, since it is a programmer error rather than a data case.
A vanished persona pool raises at initialize time, so the manager does not trust the config loader's earlier check.
Applying interactions appends stance history and keeps memory_window to the agent's own most recent 5 interaction ids.
Mutating the manager after a snapshot leaves the snapshot unchanged, which is what the deep copy guarantees.
Restoring reproduces every agent exactly, and the restored manager is isolated from the passed-in list.

groups.summary: Save and load round-tripping, that a second save leaves only the latest, that a corrupt checkpoint raises, and that no .tmp file survives a successful write.

tests.summary: No checkpoint returns None, which is how a fresh run is detected.
A saved checkpoint reloads with its run id, turn and full agent state intact.
A second save replaces the first, since only the latest resume point is ever needed.
A corrupt checkpoint raises rather than silently restarting at turn 0 and discarding completed work.
save creates its own checkpoints directory, unlike the logging writer.
The temporary file is gone after a successful save, confirming the write-then-rename completed.
The checkpoint on disk is valid JSON, so the atomic rename did not leave it torn.

groups.summary: Every config rejection path, including that two independent errors both surface in one ConfigLoadError, that YAML-supplied git_commit_hash is ignored, and that unknown keys are named.

tests.summary: A valid config loads into an ExperimentRun with git_commit_hash resolved from the working tree.
A hash written into the YAML is discarded and replaced by the real HEAD, so a config cannot claim a commit it did not run against.
A nonexistent config path raises ConfigLoadError rather than an OSError.
Unparseable YAML surfaces as ConfigLoadError, keeping the documented contract that every failure is one error type.
A missing required field is named in the error message rather than reported generically.
N greater than or equal to M is rejected at load time.
Memes enabled with no pool id fails on the schema validator, before any filesystem lookup is attempted.
A meme pool id that resolves to no file is rejected, and the error names the path it looked for.
A meme-enabled config pointing at the real fixture pool loads cleanly.
A config with a bad field and a missing asset reports both in one ConfigLoadError. This is why errors accumulate instead of failing fast, a deliberate deviation from the design doc's sample.
A missing persona pool is reported on its own, so the asset check does not depend on schema validation having failed.
Any mode but multi_turn is rejected, since there is exactly one simulation mode.
YAML that parses to a list, string or number is rejected as ConfigLoadError rather than crashing on the dict operations that follow.
The error names the config the caller passed, not the placeholder path the git-hash helper raises with.
The missing-file error names the real path too.
Errors render as 'field: message' rather than raw Pydantic dicts, which repeated the whole input payload once per error.
An unknown key is reported by name with a typo hint, rather than as the bare extra_forbidden type.

groups.summary: Cost arithmetic and accumulation, that an unpriced combination raises instead of charging zero, ceiling behaviour, and that concurrent record() calls lose no updates.

tests.summary: Cost is computed from the per-1k rates and accumulates across calls.
An unpriced provider, model or modality raises ValueError rather than charging zero and understating the run's cost.
The breaching call is counted before CostCeilingExceeded is raised, so the reported total includes it.
With no ceiling configured, no total ever raises.
Text and vision calls are priced from their own rate entries.
Many threads recording at once produce the exact expected total, so no update is lost.
A missing pricing table raises FileNotFoundError when the tracker is built, before any call is made.

groups.summary: The builders themselves: that their defaults validate, that overrides still go through validation, and that the mock gateway both returns a parseable reply and rejects calls breaking the real signature.

tests.summary: The run builder's defaults validate and individual fields can be overridden.
An invalid override still raises, so the builder cannot be used to construct an impossible run.
make_agent accepts id and stance positionally, the shape the interaction-engine tests rely on.
The default interaction is a valid generated-text row.
Passing content_type and meme_id together builds a valid meme row.
A meme row with no meme_id is rejected by the model's own validator, not papered over by the builder.
A failed_logged_null row can be built, and reports itself as invalid for analysis.
The builder's reply text parses through the real parser, so mocked replies match what production accepts.
The default backend response body parses.
A text override produces a body the parser rejects, which is how the retry path is driven.
The mock gateway fixture returns something the orchestrator can actually consume.
The mock rejects a call that would not match the real signature. This pins the autospec behaviour, since replacing generate with a bare AsyncMock still works but silently stops catching drift.
The text-only fixture reports supports_vision False, so the fallback path is actually exercised.

groups.summary: End to end, YAML on disk to interactions.jsonl: the shipped example config loads, a full run writes correct output, the same seed reproduces a run exactly, a resumed run matches an uninterrupted one, and agent state agrees with the log.

tests.summary: configs/example_run.yaml loads through the real loader, so the documented example cannot rot unnoticed.
The example config's commented-out meme block validates when enabled, so the documented snippet actually works.
The whole path from a YAML file to all four output files, with only the LLM call faked. The first test to exercise more than one production module together.
A meme-enabled run produces rows whose content_type, meme_id and stance all come from the dataset.
Re-running a finished config writes nothing further, the resume behaviour the launcher documents.
Two runs on one seed produce byte-identical logs on the fields that matter, the end-to-end reproducibility claim.
Each agent's final stance_history matches the rows logged for it, so the two outputs cannot disagree.
A run interrupted and resumed produces the same output as one that never stopped, which is what the per-turn derived streams and the rebuilt last-posts map exist to guarantee.
Every column the planned analysis tier needs is present and populated on each row, checked before that tier exists.
prompt_token_count is populated on text rows, the column that makes the per-language prompt-length gap measurable at all.

groups.summary: Alpha extremes (homophilous at 1, roughly uniform at 0), the N-distinct-never-self contract, seeded reproducibility, and that zero, negative, NaN and mismatched sampling weights all raise.

tests.summary: An alpha below 0 or above 1 raises at construction rather than being clamped into range.
An N below 1 raises at construction.
At alpha 1 the selected neighbours are the closest-stance candidates, the maximally homophilous end of the mechanism.
At alpha 0, selection frequency across many seeds is roughly uniform, the no-echo-chamber end.
Every draw returns exactly N distinct agents and never the speaker, the contract the protocol states.
Fewer than N candidates raises ValueError rather than returning a short list.
Identically seeded streams produce identical neighbour sets.
At turn 1 the engine reads initial_stance even for an agent that somehow has history, which is what keeps the frozen-snapshot reading well defined.
A zero weight raises, since the sampling key formula divides by it.
A negative weight raises. It is worse than an error: it would sort first and be guaranteed selected, a silent wrong answer in the module whose contract is to never clamp.
A NaN weight raises, since it would make the sort order meaningless.
Mismatched weight and item counts raise rather than silently truncating.

groups.summary: That concurrent appends produce N untorn parseable lines, that both one-shot writes round-trip through their models, that agents_final overwrites, and that a missing run_dir raises.

tests.summary: Many concurrent appends produce exactly N parseable lines with none torn, which is what the lock is for.
run_config.json reloads into an equivalent ExperimentRun.
agents_final.jsonl holds one parseable Agent line per agent.
A second call leaves only the second list, confirming overwrite rather than append.
Writing into a directory that does not exist raises, since creating the run directory is the orchestrator's job.

groups.summary: Injection decisioning across disabled, rate 0, rate 1 and fixed-turn schedules, seeded reproducibility, the empty and missing pool error paths, and that every image path in the real pool resolves on disk.

tests.summary: With injection disabled every speaker gets None even at rate 1.0, and no pool is loaded at all.
Rate 0 injects nothing across many turns.
Rate 1 under the random schedule injects for every speaker on every turn.
Under fixed_turn, injection happens only on the configured turns and nowhere else.
Two managers with identically seeded streams make the same per-agent injection decisions.
A pool file that parses to no records raises ValueError at construction rather than yielding an unsamplable empty pool.
A missing pool file raises FileNotFoundError at construction.
Every image path in the shipped fixture pool exists on disk. A pre-flight audit found two missing, which would have raised for roughly two sampled memes in three.

groups.summary: Retry versus fatal classification, construction-time vision resolution, cost recording with the bare model id and correct modality, that latency is measured rather than read off the response, api_base forwarding, and that the concurrency cap holds including across retries.

tests.summary: A transient error followed by a success retries and returns the successful response.
An authentication error raises FatalGatewayError immediately, with exactly one provider call.
An unknown model id raises at construction rather than defaulting to text-only and silently misclassifying a vision model.
A call with no image records cost under the text modality.
A call with image bytes records cost under the vision modality.
release is called exactly once after a successful call.
release still runs exactly once when the provider call raises, since it sits in a finally block.
Cost is recorded under the bare model id, not the prefixed one. Passing the prefixed form looked up a doubly-qualified key and failed for every model but a bare OpenAI one.
Every model in the pricing table prices successfully through a real tracker.
Latency comes from the gateway's own clock, matching the elapsed time rather than any provider field.

A response lacking the field the design doc's sample reads still works. Reading it raised AttributeError, which neither error class covers, so it would have aborted the whole run on the first successful call.
Every self-hosted, Ollama and free-tier model id in the vision tables constructs without raising.
A configured api_base reaches the litellm call, which is the only way a local server is reachable at all.
With no api_base configured, None is forwarded, leaving hosted-provider routing unchanged.
Every model id the vision tables recognize that is meant to be runnable has a pricing entry, so a run cannot die at record() time.
With a cap configured, in-flight requests never exceed it. Without the cap a turn opens M connections and the surplus accumulates until the server starts closing them.
With no cap, concurrency rises above any single-digit bound, preserving the previous behaviour for hosted providers.
Capping delays requests without dropping any: every call still completes.
A retrying call holds its slot rather than taking a second one, so retries cannot push past the cap.

groups.summary: Schema-level guarantees: the memory_window cap on construction and on assignment, that in-place append bypasses it, extra=forbid on both config models, and that a stance_scale of two identical values is rejected.

tests.summary: A memory_window of 6 entries is rejected at construction by the field's own length cap.
Assigning an over-cap memory_window raises, which is what validate_assignment exists for: without it the cap would hold only by convention in calling code.
Assigning exactly 5 entries is accepted, so the cap is inclusive.
Documents the known limit: appending in place grows the list past 5 because Pydantic cannot observe mutation. This is why the prompt builder re-slices at the point of use.
validate_assignment applies to every field, not just memory_window: an empty persona is rejected on assignment too.
current_stance returns initial_stance with no history, and the last recorded value once there is one.
An unrecognized top-level config key raises rather than being silently absorbed into a default.
An unrecognized key inside the meme block raises too, the case that would otherwise turn RQ3's meme arm into a second control arm.
Forbidding extras does not break the legitimate optional fields, which still load.
A scale of two identical values is rejected, since min equals max would make every reply but one unparseable.
Two distinct values satisfy the validator, so the check counts distinct values rather than demanding more entries.

groups.summary: That the three language conditions differ only in the directive line and stay within a bounded length spread, the Fix A five-turn memory slice, turn-1 neighbour omission, the one-image meme rule and its downgrade flag, and that a retry changes only the format block.

tests.summary: English, Hinglish and Hindi all produce a prompt containing their own directive.
Prompts for two conditions are identical except the directive line, which is what keeps RQ1's comparison unconfounded by prompt shape.
The three directives stay within a bounded length of each other, so no condition carries a systematically longer instruction.
On a full prompt with memory and neighbours the between-condition length difference is negligible, bounding the confound at the point the model sees it.
An unknown condition raises rather than quietly rendering as English, which would make a misconfigured run look valid.
A reply following the prompt's own format parses cleanly through the real parser, so the two contracts actually agree.
The format block tells the model to put the number on the STANCE line only, because the parser strips every occurrence from the reason text.
The rendered bounds come from the configured scale rather than being hardcoded.
Both anchor labels appear, so a bare number means the same thing to every agent on every turn.
With more than five history entries only the last five render.
The slice still holds when history was grown by in-place append, which the schema cannot catch. This is the cap that actually reaches the model.
A short history renders all of it, not a padded five.
With no history the memory section is absent rather than an empty heading.
Turn 1 has no neighbour block, since bare initial stances with no reasoning would be a stimulus with no analogue later.
Later turns render each neighbour's id, position and reasoning.
A meme neighbour on a vision backend yields image bytes alongside the text.
On a text-only backend the meme becomes caption text with no image, and the fallback flag is set.
The text-only path builds successfully for a meme whose image is absent, proving no disk read happens.
With two meme neighbours exactly one image is attached and the flag records that the other degraded, since the gateway takes only one image.
An all-text neighbour set yields no image and no fallback flag.
The rendered meme framing matches what vision_fallback produces, so the wording is not duplicated here and cannot drift.
A neighbour post naming an unknown meme id raises, surfacing a disagreement between the log and the pool.
A retry changes only the format block. Altering persona, topic, memory or neighbours would mean the logged row answers a different stimulus than a first attempt, mixing two conditions in one dataset.
The emphasised block still describes a format the real parser accepts.
Building leaves the agent and neighbour posts untouched, which matters because the caller passes the frozen snapshot.
A whole-number stance renders as an integer while a fractional one keeps its decimal.

groups.summary: Interval spacing, that an unconfigured provider returns immediately, that concurrent acquires for one provider serialize, and that a limit of 0 means no limit rather than a division by zero.

tests.summary: Successive acquires for one provider are separated by at least 60/limit seconds.
A provider absent from the limits dict is unlimited and returns without waiting.
Concurrent acquires for one provider serialize through its lock and stay interval-spaced.
A configured limit of 0 means no limit, rather than dividing by zero or blocking every request.
release changes no state, confirming it exists only for call-site symmetry.

groups.summary: That one seed reproduces each stream, that the three streams never correlate, that a property returns the same advancing instance, and that turn_rng is a pure function of seed, purpose and turn so a resume replays nothing.

tests.summary: Two managers built from one seed produce identical neighbour-stream draws.
The same holds for the meme-injection stream.
The three offset streams produce different sequences from the same base seed, which is what the deliberate offsets are for.
Each property returns the same object every time, not a fresh Random, so the stream can advance.
Accessing a property repeatedly keeps advancing the stream rather than restarting it.
turn_rng returns the same sequence for the same seed, purpose and turn regardless of what was drawn before, which is what makes a resumed turn identical.
Demonstrates the defect turn_rng exists to fix: a rebuilt long-lived stream replays turn 1's draws, because its position was never checkpointed.
Derived streams differ across turns and across purposes, so no two collide.
Two runs sharing a seed still draw identically from derived streams, which is what holds neighbour sampling constant while language varies.
An unknown purpose or a turn below 1 raises ValueError rather than silently producing a stream.

groups.summary: The widest file: per-turn row counts and neighbour shape, seeded reproducibility, meme turns costing no call, the parse-retry and fatal-error paths, cost-ceiling and unexpected-exception aborts, checkpoint intervals, resume, and that no agent sees another's same-turn output.

tests.summary: A completed run writes exactly M times K rows.
Every logged row carries exactly N neighbour ids and never the speaker's own.
A completed run leaves both agents_final.jsonl and a checkpoint on disk.
The orchestrator creates the run directory itself, which the logging writer deliberately does not do.
Turn 1 prompts carry no neighbour block, since nobody has posted yet.
Turn 2 prompts carry the neighbours' turn-1 posts.
Two runs on one seed produce identical neighbour draws throughout.
Different seeds produce different neighbour draws, confirming the seed is actually consumed.
Meme turns make no gateway call and take their stance from the dataset label, which is what makes memes a content-replacement mechanism rather than a prompt change.
A neighbour's meme arrives at a vision backend as attached image bytes.
A text-only backend records used_vision_fallback on the rows that saw a meme as caption only.
A persistently unparseable reply is retried to the budget, then logged as failed_logged_null rather than given a fabricated stance.
A reply that parses on a later attempt is logged as retried_success, so retries stay visible in the dataset.
A failed agent's stance_after repeats stance_before and no history is appended, so later turns keep reading its last known value.
A fatal gateway error fails one agent's turn and the rest of the population continues.
A fatal error produces exactly one provider call, confirming it is outside the retry policy.
A cost ceiling breach aborts the run instead of being absorbed per agent. The design doc's sample swallowed it, contradicting its own statement that it is fatal.
An unanticipated exception type propagates and aborts, so a real bug surfaces loudly rather than becoming a soft-failure row.
An abort after at least one completed turn records failed_partial, so the run does not look like it is still running.
A completed run rewrites run_config.json with status, timestamps and total cost.
Checkpoints are written on the configured interval rather than every turn.
A final turn the interval would skip is checkpointed anyway, since otherwise a completed run would resume from the wrong place.
Re-running a completed run adds no rows and makes no calls, because the checkpoint already covers turn K.
A run resumed from a mid-run checkpoint continues at the next turn rather than restarting.
A resumed run rebuilds each agent's last post from the log including its meme content, which agent state alone cannot express and which would otherwise change the stimulus mid-run.
The logged stance_before matches what the interaction engine reads. If they disagreed, every regression fitted on that column would be wrong.
Each turn's stance_before equals the previous turn's stance_after for that agent.
No prompt in a turn contains any reasoning produced in that same turn, the direct check on the frozen-snapshot guarantee that reproducibility rests on.
A failed turn is written to the log, since a failure is data rather than a gap.
A failed turn appends no StanceRecord, so no blank reasoning enters the agent's history.
Neighbours of a failed agent are shown its last real post rather than an empty contribution.

A failed turn consumes none of the agent's five memory slots. Otherwise a language condition with more parse failures would systematically receive less context, which is the asymmetry the memory cap exists to prevent.
Across three attempts the prompt is built at most twice, since only a plain and an emphasised variant exist. Rebuilding per attempt re-read the meme image from disk each time.

groups.summary: Well-formed and malformed STANCE lines, case insensitivity, negative and decimal values, that the first of several matches wins while all are stripped from reason_text, and the scale range checks.

tests.summary: A well-formed reply yields the value, and the STANCE line is removed from the reason text.
A reply with no STANCE line raises StanceParseFailure.
A non-numeric value raises StanceParseFailure.
Negative and decimal stances parse, so the pattern is not limited to positive integers.
Lower and mixed case stance labels parse.
With several STANCE substrings the first supplies the value and every one is stripped, so a restated stance cannot leak into the field the RQ2 analyses read.
An in-range value is returned unchanged, so nothing is rounded to a scale point.
A value below the scale raises rather than being clamped to the minimum.
A value above the scale raises rather than being clamped to the maximum.

groups.summary: That a vision receiver gets matching image bytes, that a text-only receiver gets the caption woven in with no image, and that the text-only path never touches the filesystem even for a nonexistent image.

tests.summary: A vision receiver gets prompt text plus the exact bytes of the file on disk.
A text-only receiver gets no image and the caption woven into the prompt text.
A missing image raises for a vision receiver, treated as a meme-pool integrity problem.
The text-only branch succeeds even when the image does not exist, proving it never reads the file.
